requirements.label: 120 Total Credits
requirements.hint: The BSI requires 120 U-M credits in total.

requirements.label: Upper level credits (60)
requirements.hint: Half of the 120 credits must be upper level. SI 201 and SI 261 count as upper level even though they carry 200 numbers.

requirements.label: UMSI credits (54)
requirements.hint: 54 of the 120 credits must come from School of Information courses. Equivalents used to waive prerequisites, such as EECS 183 or EECS 280, do not count toward this total. UMSI courses must be taken for a letter grade of C- or higher except SI 210, SI 300, and SI 390.

requirements.label: Programming prerequisite (SI 101)
requirements.hint: SI 101 or an equivalent programming course, completed before entering the program. EECS 183, ENGR 101, and ROB 102 fulfill it but do not count toward the 54 UMSI credits. Preferred admission applicants need a B or better and cannot take it pass fail.

requirements.label: First year writing prerequisite
requirements.hint: ENGLISH 124 or 125 or an equivalent first year writing course, completed before entering the program.

requirements.label: SI 110: Introduction to Information Studies
requirements.hint: Core for all BSI students. Often taken before admission; students who have not taken it complete it in their first BSI semester.

requirements.label: SI 201: Data-Oriented Programming
requirements.hint: Core for all BSI students. EECS 280 or EECS 281 with a C or higher waives it, but waiver credits do not count toward the UMSI or upper level totals.

requirements.label: SI 261: Introduction to Statistics with Applications
requirements.hint: Core for all BSI students. Counts as upper level credit.

requirements.label: SI 300: Career and Internship Studio
requirements.hint: Core for all BSI students. One credit, and one of the few UMSI courses that may be taken pass fail.

requirements.label: SI 307: Introduction to Design
requirements.hint: UX Design capstone prerequisite. Must be taken for a letter grade.

requirements.label: SI 357: Introduction to Development
requirements.hint: UX Design capstone prerequisite. Must be taken for a letter grade.

requirements.label: SI 347: Human-Computer Interaction
requirements.hint: UX Design capstone prerequisite. Must be taken for a letter grade.

requirements.label: SI 303: Introduction to Qualitative Methods and Research
requirements.hint: UX Design capstone prerequisite. Must be taken for a letter grade.

requirements.label: SI 313: Introduction to Quantitative Methods and Research
requirements.hint: UX Design capstone prerequisite. Must be taken for a letter grade.

requirements.label: Advanced selectives (choose 2)
requirements.hint: Two of SI 407 Advanced Design, offered fall only, SI 457 Advanced Development, SI 403 Advanced Qualitative Methods and Research, or SI 413 Advanced Quantitative Methods and Research, offered winter only.

requirements.label: SI 487: UX Design Capstone I
requirements.hint: Fall of the final year. The capstone sequence must be taken in direct sequence.

requirements.label: SI 497: UX Design Capstone II
requirements.hint: Winter of the final year, immediately after SI 487.
